## Why

I chose a single, worn **collection box** as the sculptural subject because it perfectly encapsulates the Pope's primary response to the "new scourge" of unemployment. Instead of abstractly representing the economic crisis or the complex idea of "Crusade," I focused on the specific, practical mechanism the document calls for: collecting and distributing alms through the Church to directly aid the poor and children. This object is instantly recognizable as a "devotional item/sacred object" for charity, fitting the selection rubric, and rejects any abstract representation of the broader theological concepts by centering the concrete, physical tool for the "Crusade of piety and of love." A single collection box allows for an isolated, highly detailed render on a transparent background, satisfying the single-subject and isolation tests.

The selection of the collection box provides a strong, concrete representation of the document's call for charitable works, and the text explanation supports this choice well. However, the resulting image has failed to meet the specific technical constraints provided. The prompt explicitly mandated a transparent background, but the generation includes a baked-in checker pattern instead. Furthermore, the instructions strictly prohibited any text or lettering on the sculpture, yet the text 'CRUSADE OF CHARITY' appears prominently on the front. I am regenerated the image to correct these technical errors by enforcing a truly transparent background and ensuring the object is free from any text inscriptions.

To translate this vision into the final sculptural form, I will adjust the model to target a clean, high-end 3D render while meticulously addressing the technical constraints and the stylistic requirements of Nova Impendet. I will begin by eliminating the baked-in checkerboard pattern and replacing it with true transparency, using an alpha channel to ensure a flawless isolated result. Next, I must remove all text, specifically the "CRUSADE OF CHARITY" inscription, and fill that area with smooth, dark wood texture that is perfectly consistent with the surrounding aged grain. To enhance the relief, I will raise and broaden the carved hand symbols to emphasize the theological themes of aid and charity. Finally, I will strictly adhere to the established visual parameters by using a 3/4 high-contrast angle, dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, and a polished granite plinth to complete this luxury sacred-object finish.

# Sculptural form: The Charity Box of Nova Impendet

## Concept
The collection box is the essential material translation of Nova Impendet, transforming the abstract theological concepts of a "Crusade of love" and the moral response to the financial crisis into a single, instantly recognizable object of Catholic devotional life. While the encyclical addresses complex themes of mass unemployment, children's suffering, and the proliferation of arms, this single form rejects abstract geometry in favor of a concrete vessel for alms, which Pius XI explicitly named as the immediate solution to the crisis. By isolating the box with a high-end, Cinema 4D-style render on a transparent background, the sculpture emphasizes the Church’s pragmatic role as the dispenser of charity—where the act of giving to the box is directly equated, through the Gospel, to giving to Christ. This single-subject approach is necessary for clarity in a text-to-image model, as any attempt at a multi-symbol composition (combining bread, broken chains, and monetary crisis symbols) would result in a incoherent conceptual cluster rather than a potent sacred object.

## Text-to-image prompt
A premium, physically-based 3D render (Octane style, Cinema 4D) of a solitary, aged wooden collection box on a minimalist dark granite plinth, set against a transparent background. The sculpture is seen from a three-quarter angle, emphasizing its form and texture. The box is constructed of distressed, dark-stained oak with deep grain and procedural wear, reinforced by tarnished, hammer-marked wrought iron straps and corner brackets, secured with visible, worn rivets. The lid is slightly domed, featuring a narrow coin slot. The frontal panel contains a deep-relief carving of a Madonna and Child, depicted with a worn, aged wood finish. Directly below this relief, the smooth wooden panel is entirely bare, with no text or inscriptions, leaving only a clean, seamless surface where the words "CRUSADE OF CHARITY" were previously located, matching the color and texture of the surrounding wood. At the very bottom of the front panel, two carved hands reach upwards in a gesture of receiving, slightly raised and broader than before to emphasize their symbolic function. The overall geometry is refined, with procedural microtextures on both the wood and metal surfaces. Dramatic, cinematic lighting from the upper left casts deep shadows and emphasizes the contours of the relief and the texture of the materials, with global illumination and ray-traced reflections providing depth. A strong rim light from the right defines the silhouette. Aperture f/11, 85mm lens. No text is visible on the image.
